\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{محض} (mahz)}{محض (mahz)}]{\ur{محض} (mahz) — mere; merely}

\label{lesson:UR-C367-mahz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for on no account, then the Urdu for to forbid.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{محض}}
\textbf{\ur{محض}} — \emph{mahz} — \textquotedblleft{}mere; merely\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{یہ} \ur{محض} \ur{غلط} \ur{فہمی} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{کوئی} \ur{بات} \ur{نہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar yih mahz ghalat-fahmī hai to koī bāt nahīṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If this is a mere misunderstanding, it does not matter.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{محض}} (\emph{mahz}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{maḥḍ}, \textquotedblleft{}pure, sheer\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mahz}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mahz}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar yih mahz ghalat-fahmī hai to koī bāt nahīṅ.} — If this is a mere misunderstanding, it does not matter.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for on no account, then the Urdu for to forbid, then say \emph{mahz} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{محض} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Mere; merely\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{قاعدہ} (qāidā)}{قاعدہ (qāidā)}]{\ur{قاعدہ} (qāidā) — a rule; a regulation}

\label{lesson:UR-C367-qaida}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to forbid, then the Urdu for mere.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{قاعدہ}}
\textbf{\ur{قاعدہ}} — \emph{qāidā} — \textquotedblleft{}a rule; a regulation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{قاعدہ} \ur{یہی} \ur{ہے} \ur{تو} \ur{ہم} \ur{کیا} \ur{کر} \ur{سکتے} \ur{ہیں؟}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar qāidā yihī hai to ham kyā kar sakte haiṅ?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If that is the rule, what can we do?
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{قاعدہ}} (\emph{qāidā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{qāʿida}, \textquotedblleft{}a base, a foundation; a rule\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qāidā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qāidā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar qāidā yihī hai to ham kyā kar sakte haiṅ?} — If that is the rule, what can we do?
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to forbid, then the Urdu for mere, then say \emph{qāidā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{قاعدہ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A rule; a regulation\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{خلاف} \ur{ورزی} (khilāf-varzī)}{خلاف ورزی (khilāf-varzī)}]{\ur{خلاف} \ur{ورزی} (khilāf-varzī) — a breach; a violation}

\label{lesson:UR-C367-khilaf-varzi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for mere, then the Urdu for a regulation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{خلاف} \ur{ورزی}}
\textbf{\ur{خلاف} \ur{ورزی}} — \emph{khilāf-varzī} — \textquotedblleft{}a breach; a violation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{قانون} \ur{کی} \ur{خلاف} \ur{ورزی} \ur{ہوئی} \ur{تو} \ur{جرمانہ} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar qānūn kī khilāf-varzī huī to jurmānā ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the law is broken, there will be a fine.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{خلاف} \ur{ورزی}} (\emph{khilāf-varzī}) is built from \textbf{\ur{خلاف}}, \textquotedblleft{}against\textquotedblright{}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{khilāf}, and Persian \emph{varzī}, \textquotedblleft{}practising\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{varzīdan}. Acting against a rule.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khilāf-varzī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar qānūn kī khilāf-varzī huī to jurmānā ho gā.} — If the law is broken, there will be a fine.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for mere, then the Urdu for a regulation, then say \emph{khilāf-varzī} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{شق} (shiq)}{شق (shiq)}]{\ur{شق} (shiq) — a clause (in an agreement)}

\label{lesson:UR-C367-shiq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a regulation, then the Urdu for a breach.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{شق}}
\textbf{\ur{شق}} — \emph{shiq} — \textquotedblleft{}a clause (in an agreement)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{آپ} \ur{اس} \ur{شق} \ur{سے} \ur{متفق} \ur{نہیں} \ur{تو} \ur{بتائیے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar āp is shiq se muttafiq nahīṅ to batāiye.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you do not agree with this clause, say so.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{شق}} (\emph{shiq}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{shiqq}, \textquotedblleft{}a split; one of two halves\textquotedblright{}; Urdu uses it for a clause of a written agreement or a law, a sense our sources do not trace.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shiq}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shiq}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar āp is shiq se muttafiq nahīṅ to batāiye.} — If you do not agree with this clause, say so.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a regulation, then the Urdu for a breach, then say \emph{shiq} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{شق} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A clause (in an agreement)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نافذ} \ur{ہونا} (nāfiz honā)}{نافذ ہونا (nāfiz honā)}]{\ur{نافذ} \ur{ہونا} (nāfiz honā) — to come into force; to take effect}

\label{lesson:UR-C367-nafiz-hona}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a breach, then the Urdu for a clause.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نافذ} \ur{ہونا}}
\textbf{\ur{نافذ} \ur{ہونا}} — \emph{nāfiz honā} — \textquotedblleft{}to come into force; to take effect\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{نیا} \ur{قانون} \ur{نافذ} \ur{ہوا} \ur{تو} \ur{کرایہ} \ur{بڑھے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar nayā qānūn nāfiz huā to kirāyā baṛhe gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the new law comes into force, rents will rise.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{قانون} \ur{نافذ} \ur{ہو} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh qānūn nāfiz ho gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{نافذ} \ur{ہونا}} (\emph{nāfiz honā}) is built from \emph{nāfiz}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{nāfidh}, \textquotedblleft{}piercing; effective\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{ہونا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to be\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nāfiz honā}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a breach, then the Urdu for a clause, then say \emph{nāfiz honā} again
\end{itemize}
